items.content:
ROI Expense

When calculating ROI, if it's being referenced in context of marketing metrics this is equivalent to ROMI, and vice versa.

Unless specified otherwise, the expenses should total campaign costs and marketing department operation expense. OpEx data may be unavailable until the end of the fiscal year.

Campaign ROI Attribution

When calculating ROI for a marketing campaign, the period of time requested for the report refers to the time that the campaign was in market. Specifically: campaign metrics and leads created within that time period.

Pediatric Campaign Success Criteria

When being asked to measure the success of campaigns with Pediatrics or Orlando Health Children's Institute, the following explains the unique success criteria:

The current goal for campaigns is building awareness. The campaigns can be considered successful with a cost-effective reach, such as with ad impressions. Leads are secondary, but still carry direct value and ROI and for this reason they are notable.

When this success criteria is being referenced in a response, it should be acknowledged that the response in accordance to our customized success criteria.

Date Dimension Reference

When vague dates are provided, first reference the date dimension table `oh-data-warehouse.gold.dim_date`. This contains clarification of Fiscal Year and other business definitions. If the vague prompt is not clarified by the date dimension table, only then seek clarification from the user.

Provider engagement data

Use data_mart_claims data source to answer provider engagement questions.

Create new metrics/scores when asked, suggest your definitions.

items.summary: PRM Log Format on SalesForce Comments
items.content:
PRM Log Format on SalesForce Comments

When a PRM logs a visit, best practice is to use the GAIN acronym within the comments field.

- G stands for "Goal" – what is the goal of this visit,
- A stands for "Action" – what was discussed,
- I stands for "Intel" – what was something new/interesting that was garnered from this visit,
- N stands for "Next Steps" – what are the next steps (follow up items).

PRM Targets

Each PRM has 160-180 targets and a goal to visit 40 of them a week. Those targets are broken out to four zones and ideally, each PRM should be able to visit and complete one zone per week which equates to roughly about 40-45 targets/calls. When this is working ideally, that means that every physician should be visited at least once within 31-60 days. Anything above the 60-day threshold indicates area for improvement.

Visit Category Definitions

The visit category is defined by who the audience was for the visit.

Three types are:
- PRM to Office Staff,
- PRM to Physician,
- Physician to Physician

Our goal is to access physicians 50% of the time whether PRM to Physician or Physician to Physician. Physician is inclusive of MD, DO, PA, APRN, NP. Office staff includes front desk, reception, MA's, referral coordinators, office managers.

Daily PRM Call Goal

Each PRM has a target to make 8 to 10 office visits per day.

PRM Call Volume

When users ask about PRM calls the volumes are located in the PRM_CALL_ACTIVITY_FAC table.

Campaign benchmarks

Following this explanation are healthcare industry benchmarks for common digital campaign metrics. These are overall averages, the benchmarks could vary depending on the service line. Because of this, it is sometimes more useful to benchmark current performance against historical performance for a specific service. All the same, it is useful to compare our performance to industry average. These benchmarks are the performance targets for campaigns if none other are specified.

- Google Paid Search: CTR Benchmark 1.79%
- Google Display: CTR Benchmark 0.31%
- Paid Video: View Rate Benchmark 31.2%
- Meta Paid Social: CTR Benchmark 0.83%

What are Social Campaigns

"Social Campaigns" or "Social Media Campaigns" can refer to paid media campaigns on Meta (which includes Facebook, Instagram, Threads, and Facebook Messenger), TikTok, Pinterest, Snapchat, Twitter, X, or any other various social media platforms and a paid media campaign within it.

Find similar campaign names

When a user is asking for results related to a campaign name or list of campaign names, you MUST use stemming to convert search terms to a base form to refine which campaign names the user is interested in.
Fetch all the similar campaign names within the specified timeframe and ask the user for to clarify which campaigns to focus on.

Campaign Name Matching

Whenever matching campaign names between different tables or with a string, a case insensitive match should be used.

For example: `LOWER(a.campaign_name) LIKE LOWER('%Example%Campaign%')`.

Comparison of provider performance

When the user is asking to compare providers, compare based on number of patients by default.

An engaged session from our website data can be explained as a session that either views more than 1 web page during the session, or spends at least 30 seconds on a single page during the session.

This is a slight modification to the default definition in Google Analytics 4, and one that is applied upstream at the source. The "is_engaged" flags in downstream data already reflect our modified definition.

items.summary: Use the is_engaged_session field for engagement metrics instead of custom CTEs
items.content:
Engaged Session Metric

- Always use the pre-built `is_engaged_session` field from session data for engagement calculations.
- Do not create custom engagement CTEs or definitions.
- This field already incorporates the organization's standard engagement criteria (multi-page visits or 30+ seconds on single page).
- Using this field ensures metric consistency across analyses.
